articleTitle: A Predictive of Student's Interest in Game Learning Using Data Mining Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: The purpose of this research is to create a model that predicts learners' interest in gaming-based learning using data mining techniques. The study involved 304 students from the Business Computer Program at Suphan Buri Vocational College, Thailand. Using the Rapid Miner Studio (version 10.3.001) and a decision tree algorithm, the research classified students' interest based on their gaming habits, study experience with games, and academic performance. Results revealed that students who enjoy playing games, have studied using games, and have not passed all subjects are more likely to be interested in gaming learning. In contrast, those who passed all subjects are less interested. The model's accuracy, evaluated by splitting the data into training (70%) and testing (30%) sets, was 86.81%. These findings can inform the development of educational games to enhance classroom interaction, improve cognitive and affective skills, and stimulate learners' interest in innovative learning methods.

articleTitle: Malware Detection and Analysis Using Deep Learning Through Fully Connected Neural Network (FCNN)
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This research focuses on malware detection and analysis using deep learning techniques through Fully Connected Neural Network (FCNN) to enhance detection accuracy and reduce false alarm rates. The study emphasizes developing a model capable of efficiently detecting malware attacks in complex network environments. The model utilizes features including Source IP, Destination IP, Protocol, Source Port, and Packet Size for prediction. Experimental results demonstrate the FCNN model's high performance in data classification, achieving 91.49% Accuracy, 95.45% Precision, 87.50% Recall, and 91.18% F1-score. The research highlights the potential of deep learning technology in cybersecurity threat prevention and handling complex attacks, providing effective and timely responses to emerging attack patterns.

articleTitle: Leveraging Artificial Intelligence for Green Social Innovation: Enhancing Human Resource Development in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: The purpose of this paper is to present a literature study that highlights the importance of AI in driving green social innovation by focusing on human resource development in Indonesia. The approach used in writing this paper is a systematic literature review using two devices as tools, namely publish or perish and Vosviewer. The results obtained show several dynamics in Indonesia related to green social innovation and human resource development, which are unique so that they are interesting to be developed further with empirical research that can compare Indonesia with other countries.

articleTitle: The Development of a Depression Risk Assessment System Using Data Mining
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This research aimed to develop a depression risk assessment system using data mining principles. The system was developed as a web application accessible via both computers and mobile devices, utilizing the Thai version of the Center for Epidemiologic Studies Depression Scale (CES-D) as the primary screening tool, combined with data mining techniques to analyze patterns and relationships of factors contributing to depression. The system features a user-friendly interface, comprising a 20-item questionnaire assessment section and a dashboard displaying easy-to-understand analytical results. The system was tested with a sample of 400 students from the Faculty of Management Science at Phetchaburi Rajabhat University. The research findings revealed that 27.50% of students were at risk of developing depression. Analysis using Association Rule data mining techniques identified several significant factors correlated with depression. The highest risk was found among third-year students at 45%, followed by students living in off-campus accommodation (33.33%), students from divorced families (31.82%), and female students (31.58%). Additionally, analysis by academic major showed that students in Business Information Management had the highest rate of depression.

articleTitle: Copyrighted Music Detection Using Machine Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This research aims to develop a model for detecting copyrighted music using machine learning techniques and audio fingerprinting. The training data for the model were obtained from JSON files containing extracted audio features, which were processed using a 1D Convolutional Neural Network (Conv1D) architecture with Dense Layers to classify music based on MFCCs, Delta, Delta-Delta, Spectral Peaks, Spectral Flux, Harmonic Peaks, and Frame Energy. The model was improved using SMOTE to address data imbalance issues and evaluated through K-Fold Cross Validation to enhance its learning efficiency and classification accuracy. The experimental results indicate that the training accuracy ranged from 52.23% to 54.55%, while the validation accuracy varied between 51.21% and 54.79%, suggesting that the model effectively learned from the training data while maintaining stable validation performance. However, the accuracy gap indicates a degree of overfitting, requiring further improvement. Additionally, validation loss fluctuated between 1.1611 and 1.3744, as shown in Figure 2, indicating that while the model achieved lower training loss, its generalization capability remains a challenge. Evaluation through the Classification Report revealed an overall accuracy of 40.18%, demonstrating strong classification capability. The highest precision was observed for (0.57) and “Missed Call” (0.42), while the lowest recall was found in the “LONDON” class (0.31), as highlighted in Figure 1. The confusion matrix further reveals misclassification trends, particularly in overlapping classes, where was frequently misclassified as . To enhance the model's robustness, future work should focus on refining feature extraction, implementing better regularization techniques, and optimizing hyperparameters to reduce overfitting. Additionally, expanding the dataset and incorporating real-time matching techniques will further improve the system's efficiency in detecting copyrighted music in practical applications.

articleTitle: Development of Automated Pest Classification System Using Machine Learning Techniques for Smart Agriculture System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This research aims to develop an automated pest classification system using machine learning techniques. The study utilized a dataset of 6,444 images containing 17 different types of pests. Five machine learning algorithms were compared: Support Vector Machine (SVM), Neural Network, K-Nearest Neighbor, Logistic Regression, and Decision Tree. The results showed that SVM achieved the highest performance with 96.40% accuracy, demonstrating high Precision and Recall values across all classes and the largest area under the ROC curve. The evaluation was conducted using 10-fold Cross Validation. The system was further developed into an API for smart farming applications, enabling farmers to effectively identify and manage crop pests..

articleTitle: Chatbot on LINE Application Using Natural Language Processing for Providing Preliminary Solutions in the Use of Medical Equipment for Healthcare Facilities
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This research aims to develop a chatbot on the LINE platform, incorporating Natural Language Processing (NLP) techniques to provide guidance and assist in troubleshooting medical equipment usage within healthcare settings. The proposed system integrates the large language model LLAMA-3.1-8B-Instruct, a vector database, and the LINE Messaging API to enhance the chatbot's capacity to understand user queries and retrieve relevant information swiftly and accurately. The development process emphasizes enabling the chatbot to analyze the context of queries, identify pertinent information, and deliver responses that are both accurate and consistent with medical equipment manuals. The system was evaluated through a series of 30 simulated scenarios, representing common issues encountered in medical equipment use. Evaluation metrics included N-gram Precision, and the performance of the system was assessed through BLEU Score, ROUGE Score, and F1-Score. The results demonstrated that the chatbot provided correct and comprehensive responses in all cases, achieving a BLEU Score of 0.80, a ROUGE Score of 0.83, and an F1-Score of 0.81. These findings indicate that the developed chatbot system possesses significant potential to alleviate the workload of healthcare professionals, reduce the time required to locate information, and enhance the efficiency of patient services. The system provides rapid, accurate, and relevant assistance with medical equipment usage and troubleshooting, aligning with the specific needs of healthcare environments that demand both accuracy and timely responses.

articleTitle: Green and Social Innovation Behaviors Among Employees of SOEs in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: State-Owned Enterprises (SOEs) play a critical role in Indonesia's economy and sustainability agenda. SOEs contributed 21.9% of the 2023 state budget. Many of these SOEs is also pioneering green initiatives. This preliminary study investigates how trust in SOEs (organizational trust), mediated by consumer brand engagement (CBE) in social media, drives green and social innovation behavior among employees Surveying 93 respondents (87.1% SOE employees aged 18–45), this study applies an integrated framework incorporating Mayer and Davis's (1999) organizational trust model and behavioural theories. This preliminary study indicates that benevolence and trust significantly enhance CBE that contributes to green innovation behavior. However, the study found that ability and integrity dimensions of organizational trusts were not significant. These results suggest that SOEs' social responsibility and public welfare orientation are more effective at fostering engagement than perceptions of competence or ethical governance. This study suggests that CBE acts as a critical mediator between trust and sustainability behaviors, highlighting the need for active engagement to translate trust into action. This study contributes to the literature by contextualizing trust and engagement within Indonesian SOEs and emphasizes leveraging social media platforms like Instagram to promote benevolence-driven policies and trust-building initiatives. Limitations and further studies are discussed.

articleTitle: The Development of Prototype Application to Apply Augmented Reality with Alloy Wheel Business
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This research develops a prototype application that employs Augmented Reality (AR) technology to enhance the alloy wheel business in Thailand. As the automotive industry grows, the demand for customizable alloy wheels increases, yet traditional selection methods are often time-consuming. This study addresses these challenges by creating an AR application for Android devices, enabling car owners to visualize different alloy wheel designs on their vehicles in real time. Utilizing the System Development Life Cycle (SDLC), the application was developed with Blender for 3D modeling, Vuforia Engine for marker detection, and Unity for scripting. Ten alloy wheel models were created, and user satisfaction evaluations indicated a positive reception. The findings suggest that the AR application significantly improves customer experience and decision-making efficiency in selecting alloy wheels. This research highlights the potential of AR technology in the automotive aftermarket and recommends further development of additional 3D models and optimization for various devices.

articleTitle: Enhancing Job-Competency Matching: A Comparative Study of BERT-Based Approaches for Targeted Assessment
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: The rapid evolution of the labor market has intensified the complexity of matching job applicants with suitable positions. Traditional hiring methods, such as resumes and interviews, often fail to fully capture an applicant's competencies. This limitation is particularly evident as job roles become increasingly specialized, requiring a more precise evaluation of skills and knowledge.

articleTitle: E-Business Platform for Enterprise Green Logistics Management: A Case Study of Logistics Business in Bangkok, Suburban Areas, and Laem Chabang
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This research examines the gap between Thailand's green logistics aspirations and current technological capabilities, as highlighted during the 2022 APEC Summit. With the introduction of the BCG (Bio-Circular-Green) Economy Model, there is an urgent need to align logistics technology with sustainability goals. Key challenges include rising greenhouse gas emissions, maritime transportation delays, and climate change impacts, all contributing to higher operational costs. To address these issues, this study proposes the development of an electronic business platform for green logistics management and Carbon Footprint calculation, particularly in road freight operations. The platform will facilitate zero-emission truck adoption and Carbon Credit investment, creating sustainable revenue streams for the logistics sector. By enhancing logistics infrastructure and supporting E-commerce and advanced transportation technologies, this research contributes to Thailand's economic strategy and the transition toward sustainable logistics operations.

articleTitle: Analyzing the Appeal of IoT Devices in Pet Care: A Study of Applications and User Adoption
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This study examines the growing appeal and adoption of Internet of Things (IoT) devices in pet care, analyzing their applications, benefits, and challenges in modern pet management. The research investigates how IoT technology has transformed traditional pet care through smart devices such as automated feeders, health monitors, environmental control systems, and location trackers. The findings highlight that IoT pet devices attract users through several key value propositions: enhanced convenience via automation, improved pet safety and security, comprehensive health monitoring, and personalized care solutions. Moreover, the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning has facilitated predictive analytics and autonomous decision-making. However, challenges such as data privacy concerns, particularly in relation to compliance with regulations like the Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA), device reliability issues, and barriers to user adoption due to cost and usability remain significant. The study concludes that the success of IoT pet devices lies in their ability to blend technological innovation with practical solutions, thereby strengthening the bond between pets and owners and improving overall pet care standards.

articleTitle: Recurrence Dynamics of Extravasation on Computed Tomography
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: The discovery of complex patterns in extravasation on computed tomography (CT) imaging is crucial for improving the management of trauma patients. These patterns can aid in identifying complications such as vascular injury, organ rupture, or active hemorrhage, enabling timely and targeted interventions to improve patient outcomes. This study explores fuzzy logic-based nonlinear dynamic features extracted from CT imaging of extravasation, aiming to uncover radiographic patterns in trauma cases to support clinical prediction and intervention. The temporal and spatial evolution of extravasation imaging in three trauma cases are analyzed. Using geostatistics and nonlinear dynamics, this study aims to identify subtle, dynamic patterns that can enhance real-time detection and prediction of complications. These findings offer a foundation for integrating advanced imaging analytics into trauma care, improving decision-making, and optimizing patient outcomes through early intervention.

articleTitle: Development of a Contemporary Business Model Prototype for Funeral Services in Thailand Utilizing Generative AI: A New Era Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This academic study explores the development of a comprehensive funeral service business in Thailand, delivered through a mobile application and integrated with Generative AI to enhance service efficiency, speed, and cost management for the bereaved families. The integration of Generative AI allows for improved service delivery and the optimization of chatbot responses to ensure greater accuracy and relevance. The researchers anticipate that this study will assist bereaved families with no prior experience in organizing funeral ceremonies, enabling them to conduct funerals that honor the deceased in accordance with Thai cultural beliefs and traditions. The feasibility of integrating Generative AI into applications for various services has been studied [16]–[19]. The findings of these studies indicate that incorporating Generative AI enhances efficiency and reduces the operational time of the applications, subsequently increasing user demand.

articleTitle: Development of a Damage Level Classification Model for Banana Base on Image Processing and Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This study focuses on the design and development of a model to classify the levels of banana damage using image processing combined with machine learning. The dataset consists of 568 digital images of bananas, each with a resolution of 615x440 pixels, captured using a Nikon D750 camera with settings of ISO 800, 1/200 shutter speed, f/4 aperture, and a 50mm lens at a distance of approximately 25 cm from the object. The dataset categorizes banana damage into three levels: good condition 203 images, medium damage 218 images, and poor or unacceptable quality 147 images. Image processing techniques were employed to prepare the dataset, starting with converting color images to grayscale, followed by feature extraction to transform the image data into numerical data. The resulting dataset was used to create classification models, which were then evaluated using five algorithms: Multiclass Classifier Updateable, SMO, Multilayer Perceptron, Iterative Classifier Optimizer, and Random Forest. The experimental design involved splitting the data into training and testing sets using a simple random sampling approach with a 70:30 ratio. The experimental results showed the highest accuracy rates achieved by each algorithm as follows: 91.11%, 88.89%,84.44%,82.22%, and 80.00%, respectively.

articleTitle: Text Mining Algorithm for Equipment Inspection Reports via AppSheet Inspection System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This research aims to develop and analyze a risk classification model for assets using data from the 2023 fiscal year asset inspection report via the AppSheet platform, consisting of 7,000 records. The analysis, performed in RapidMiner, utilized variables such as asset type, lifespan, value, and maintenance records. K-Means Clustering grouped risks into three levels: low, medium, and high, followed by Risk Index calculation. Model performance was evaluated using 10-Fold Cross Validation, comparing six algorithms: Deep Learning, Gradient Boosted Trees, Naive Bayes, Random Forest, SVM, and XGBoost. XGBoost outperformed others with 99.39% accuracy, 0.99 Kappa, 0.61% error rate, 99.32% weighted recall, and 99.40% weighted precision. Results were visualized through a Google Looker Studio dashboard, supporting efficient risk classification and decision-making.

articleTitle: Automatic Water Filling System and Water Quality Measurement
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: Currently, excessive and unnecessary water usage is a significant issue. When water is wasted, it cannot be reused and is lost entirely, leading to various consequences. The impacts of water loss are severe, as many places around the world lack access to safe drinking water [1]. Cities often draw water from natural sources, and if these sources are not replenished, local species that rely on or inhabit these environments may perish [2]. Additionally, wastage limits the availability of water for others' needs. The visible impacts of excessive water loss are numerous. The affected ecosystems may suffer significant damage [3]. Although wastewater treatment plants exist to process and purify used water, the loss still imposes economic burdens due to the extensive resources and processes required to restore water for consumption [4]. In this study, we aim to develop an Automatic Water Filling System and Water Quality Measurement System that operates efficiently for water filtration systems [5]. To achieve this, we employed Ultrasonic Sensors, an IoT device used for distance measurement, in combination with a Solenoid Valve to control water flow, both of which are integrated into our framework. Additionally, we used TDS Measurement to determine the total dissolved solids, including inorganic and organic substances, in water. The system can be controlled via the Blynk application and provides notifications through LINE Notify. The prototype was evaluated based on criteria for water quality measurement and the results obtained from water level control.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Language Learning Platform for Thai Learners: A Design Thinking Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This research aims to develop an online language learning platform by integrating Artificial Intelligence (AI) technology and Design Thinking principles during the post-COVID-19 period, which found digital technology in education increased by 38 times compared to the pre-COVID-19 period. The study developed a platform prototype with the ability to increase learning efficiency by up to 40%, comprising an automated language level assessment system, personalized learning plan creation, and a social learning system. Testing with a sample of 47 participants revealed that the platform received 81.30% satisfaction from learners, with a mean of 4.07 and standard deviation (SD) of 0.59, and 82.70<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> satisfaction from instructors, with a mean of 4.13 and SD of 0.64. The system's core innovation is real-time learner development analysis and tracking. Organizations implementing Design Thinking innovations achieved a success rate of 75% and increased user acceptance by 40%. This research demonstrates the potential of integrating AI technology with user-centered design principles to develop educational innovations in the digital era.

articleTitle: Automated Optic Disc and Cup Segmentation Using Mask R-CNN for Glaucoma Assessment
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: Glaucoma, a leading cause of irreversible blindness, requires precise segmentation of the optic disc and optic cup in fundus images for early diagnosis and progression monitoring. This study presents an automated deep-learning-based segmentation approach using Mask R-CNN, trained on the G1020 dataset, which consists of 1,020 fundus images with corresponding labeled masks. The dataset was split into an 80% training set (816 images) and a 20% test set (204 images). The model was finetuned with a customized predictor for multiclass segmentation to effectively detect the optic disc and cup regions. Training was conducted using a stochastic gradient descent optimizer with a learning rate scheduler to enhance convergence. The proposed model achieved an average Dice coefficient of 0.9381 for the optic disc and 0.8372 for the optic cup, with corresponding Intersection over Union (IoU) scores of 0.8887 and 0.7319, demonstrating robustness in identifying these critical anatomical structures. The segmentation results show significant potential for clinical applications, aiding ophthalmologists in automated glaucoma assessment. Future work will focus on improving the model's generalizability to diverse datasets and integrating it into real-time clinical decision-making systems.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning for Anomaly and Data Breach Detection System Using Python
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This research presents the development of an anomaly and data breach detection system using Python to analyze internet traffic logs. When comparing various machine learning algorithms, it was found that Random Forest is highly effective and excels at identifying important features, which helps in clearly identifying attack detection factors. This system includes a Power BI dashboard displayed on a web window to provide actionable insights to executives and security administrators. Expert evaluations confirmed an accuracy of 90.67% along with high user satisfaction scores. This system enhances cybersecurity measures, reduces the risk of data breaches, and effectively monitors network traffic to safeguard organizational data.

articleTitle: Next-Generation Data Center Security Through IoT-Driven Surveillance
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This study evaluates the performance of various machine learning models for anomaly detection, comparing their effectiveness in identifying anomalous (−1) and normal (1) cases. The models tested include Random Forest, Isolation Forest, Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, Lasso Regression, Gradient Boosting, Quadratic Discriminant Analysis (QDA), and Deep Learning. Among the models, Random Forest, Decision Tree, and Gradient Boosting exhibit superior performance, achieving 99% accuracy with high precision, recall, and F1-scores for both anomaly and normal cases. Gradient Boosting demonstrates the lowest validation loss (0.0203), indicating high reliability. Isolation Forest and Logistic Regression show moderate effectiveness, with Isolation Forest excelling in recall for anomalies but suffering from lower precision (0.61), while Logistic Regression achieves a balanced performance (94% accuracy). Quadratic Discriminant Analysis (QDA) struggles in detecting anomalies, achieving only 0.35 recall for the anomaly class, resulting in 93% accuracy. Lasso Regression and Deep Learning perform poorly in anomaly detection, with an F1-score of 0.00 for anomalies, indicating their inability to identify such cases. Deep Learning, in particular, has the lowest overall accuracy at 79% and a high validation loss (0.2983).The results suggest that Random Forest, Decision Tree, and Gradient Boosting are the most effective models for anomaly detection, while Lasso Regression and Deep Learning demonstrate significant limitations in detecting anomalies. The findings are illustrated in Figure 1, which compares the accuracy of all models, and Figure 2, which presents the validation loss (MSE) for each model, highlighting the strengths and weaknesses of different approaches.

Index Terms: Least Absolute Shrinkage And Selection Operator

articleTitle: The System for Storing and Analyzing FM Broadcasting Content
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This research presents a prototype system for the storage and analysis of broadcast content from FM radio stations, aimed at assisting the Office of The National Broadcasting and Telecommunications Commission (Office of the NBTC) in monitoring radio programs and advertisements to ensure compliance with laws and relevant regulations. The current content verification process faces limitations in terms of resources and coverage of signal reception. The proposed prototype system utilizes Raspberry Pi 4 Model B with Software Defined Radio (SDR) to receive and record FM radio signals. The recorded audio files are conversion to text using Speech-to-Text technology, followed by content analysis through Machine Learning techniques. This system can effectively detect and identify potentially illegal content, such as misleading advertisements or inappropriate material. Test results demonstrate that the developed system performs efficiently in content recording and offers higher accuracy in content analysis compared to traditional verification methods. Additionally, it helps reduce the workload of staff, cuts travel costs, and enhances the ability to monitor a broader range of content.

articleTitle: Brain Tumor Classification System Using Decision Tree Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This research aims to study, design, and develop a brain tumor classification system using artificial intelligence, specifically decision tree algorithms. The system's primary objective is to assist medical personnel in making decisions, as distinguishing between two types of brain tumors-benign and malignant (cancerous)-can be challenging, especially for less experienced medical staff. Due to the similarities between these two types of tumors, it may be difficult for medical practitioners with limited expertise to differentiate between them in a timely manner. The proposed brain tumor classification system is designed to address this challenge. The research team conducted the study over approximately seven months, starting from the second semester of the 2023 academic year through the first semester of the 2024 academic year. Experimental results revealed that among the tree-based algorithms, Random Forest achieved the highest accuracy, followed by M5P. The best average accuracy from the experiments was obtained using a 70% training and 30% testing split, yielding an accuracy of 96.83%. Therefore, the research team selected the 70% training and 30% testing split for model development, as it provided the highest accuracy compared to the 60% training and 40% testing split, and the 80% training and 20% testing split, which showed lower accuracy. The results demonstrate that the 70% training and 30% testing approach is optimal for the brain tumor classification system, ensuring high accuracy in classifying brain tumors.

articleTitle: Optimizing Malware Detection with Random Forest, XGBoost, LightGBM, and LLM-Reporting
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This study presents a comprehensive framework for malware detection that integrates traditional machine learning algorithms with advanced large language models (LLMs) to enhance both classification accuracy and automated report generation. The proposed approach leverages three widely used machine learning models-Random Forest, XGBoost, and LightGBM-to classify different types of malwares based on extracted features from the EMBER dataset, a well-known benchmark dataset for malware analysis. Each of these models was trained and evaluated to determine their effectiveness in identifying malicious software with high accuracy. Among the tested algorithms, LightGBM exhibited the best performance, achieving an impressive classification accuracy of 83%. XGBoost followed closely with 81%, while Random Forest achieved an accuracy of 79%. To further enhance the usability of the system for cybersecurity analysts, the study incorporates a large language model, specifically LLaMA, which is accessed via an API. This model is employed to generate detailed, human-readable reports that provide insights into detected malware threats. By automating the reporting process, the framework aims to reduce the manual effort required for malware analysis, allowing security professionals to focus on high-priority threats. Future research will focus on improving classification performance through advanced feature engineering techniques and exploring deep learning-based neural network architectures to further enhance the accuracy and efficiency of malware detection and analysis.

articleTitle: Anomaly Detection in Network Traffic Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: Nowadays, cybersecurity is of utmost importance as most organizations integrate technology into their internal management systems. This integration, however, often leads to malicious attacks on these systems for various purposes, such as data theft, system disruption, or discrediting the organization. These challenges compel organizations to protect their data and systems from such malicious actors. Cyberattacks, which can severely damage organizations, are frequently executed through network intrusions. As a result, organizations need to have a network security system that can respond to threats immediately. This paper discusses an overview of cybersecurity threat prevention and network security systems, focusing on anomaly detection in network traffic using Random Forest (RF), a supervised machine learning algorithm, and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN), a deep learning technique. Additionally, it compares the performance of these two models using metrics such as Accuracy, Precision, Recall, and F1-Score to analyze their capabilities in detecting anomalies. The paper presents a comprehensive process encompassing data preparation, model training, and model evaluation. This serves as a guideline for developing robust network anomaly detection systems, ultimately enhancing organizational confidence in strengthening cybersecurity in the digital age.

articleTitle: Integrating Image Processing and Natural Language Understanding with Chatbot GPT for a Centralized Equipment Repair Notification System
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This research focuses on the development of a chatbot designed to assist with the central equipment repair notification system at King Mongkut's University of Technology North Bangkok, Rayong campus. The system operates on the LINE application platform and integrates Chatbot GPT to facilitate communication and data transmission. The chatbot utilizes advanced Artificial Intelligence (AI) techniques, specifically Natural Language Processing (NLP), to understand user input and generate contextually appropriate responses, ensuring quick and efficient interactions. Additionally, the system incorporates Image Processing techniques to verify repair notifications, ensuring the accuracy of equipment details for each repair request. The Natural Language Understanding (NLU) approach enables the chatbot to accurately interpret and respond to user queries, enhancing the overall user experience. Testing results showed that the chatbot achieved a 90% accuracy rate for text-based queries and an 85% precision rate for image verification in repair notifications. Overall, the system received high user satisfaction, demonstrating its effectiveness in improving the equipment repair notification process.

articleTitle: Phishing Email Detection Model Using Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: Phishing via email continues to be a concern in the cybersecurity realm as it exposes both individuals and companies to levels of risk due to clever social engineering methods employed by cybercriminals. This study introduces an extensive deep learning strategy for identifying phishing emails using a blend of various models such as Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU), Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT), Convolutional Neural Network (CNN), and Recurrent Neural Network (RNN). The suggested approach utilizes natural language processing and learning techniques to evaluate and categorize email material by identifying subtle attributes that differentiate valid from harmful communication effectively. Through testing and careful evaluation of the model performance, achieved results; the LSTM model attained a notable accuracy of 99.92% in detecting phishing emails. This progress highlights the promise of learning methods in addressing complex phishing threats and improving email security measures. The research offers insights into the effectiveness of neural network approaches in detecting phishing emails by comparing the performance of multiple deep learning architectures. The high level of accuracy attained indicates a path for creating smarter email security solutions that can evolve to counter cyber threats effectively.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Models for Speech-Based Depression Screening
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: Mental health issues significantly affect society, requiring long-term treatment that is both costly and impacts personal relationships. This research paper proposes a speech-based method to screen for depression risk as an accessible alternative. The research included five machine learning models-Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine (SVM), K-Nearest Neighbour (KNN), Naive Bayes, and Linear Discriminant Analysis (LDA)-were used to analyze speech data from 25 participants with varying mental health conditions. Three data preparation techniques-Leave-One-Out Cross-Validation, SMOTE, and raw data-were applied to optimize the models. Results showed that SVM with SMOTE achieved the highest accuracy (98 %), emphasizing the importance of effective data preparation. This research demonstrates the potential of using speech analysis as a cost-effective tool for early mental health screening and provides a foundation for practical applications in healthcare and beyond.

articleTitle: The Role of AI in Advancing Digital Dentistry
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is revolutionizing digital dentistry by providing innovative tools for diagnosis, treatment planning, and clinical decision-making. This narrative review explores AI's transformative role in key areas of dentistry, focusing on its ability to enhance diagnostic accuracy and optimize clinical outcomes. The applications of AI in dental imaging, diagnostics, and treatment simulations are thoroughly examined. In addition, challenges related to ethical considerations, clinical integration, and data security are addressed. This review provides a comprehensive overview of how AI is advancing digital dentistry and shaping the future of clinical practice.

articleTitle: Study Link: An Online Learning Media Application for Enhanced Educational Engagement Base on Design Thinking
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This research focuses on the development of an advanced air purifier system integrated with PM2.5 detection, UV-C light sterilization, and real-time monitoring through an IoT-based interface. The system utilizes a PM2.5 sensor to detect airborne particulate matter and activates the air purifier and UV-C light when the air quality exceeds predefined thresholds. Additionally, the system is designed to display PM2.5 values on an LCD screen and send notifications to a mobile application (LINE) to inform users about air quality conditions. Prototype testing was conducted in a 6 × 12-meter room using hairspray to simulate PM2.5 particles. The results showed that the air purifier activated successfully in response to elevated PM2.5 levels, displaying real-time data and sending alerts with messages such as “Danger” when air quality worsened. This study demonstrates the feasibility of combining IoT technology and real-time air quality monitoring to enhance environmental health management in indoor spaces. The proposed system provides a user-centric solution that not only improves air quality but also ensures immediate user awareness and intervention.

articleTitle: Grid-Based Spatial Analysis of Road Accident Patterns in Thailand
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: Road accidents in Thailand remain a significant public health concern. This study analyzes accident patterns by combining grid-based spatial analysis (0.02° × 0.02° resolution) with vehicle type distribution data from 2019–2023. Using k-means clustering, we identified eight distinct clusters, with the most critical cluster (Cluster 7) showing accident rates 5.4 times higher than the national average, particularly around Suvarnabhumi Airport. Urban centers demonstrated accident frequencies 3.2 times higher than rural areas, with private vehicles and motorcycles being the predominant vehicle types involved. Our analysis identified strong correlations between accident-prone areas and specific vehicle types, highlighting critical locations for targeted interventions such as improved road design and stricter speed regulations. These findings offer a data-driven foundation for policymakers to enhance traffic monitoring, redesign hazardous intersections, and improve infrastructure in high-risk zones.

articleTitle: Development of a Tourist Destination Recommendation Application Based on User Interests: An Application of Design Thinking
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This research aimed to develop a tourist destination recommendation application based on user interests by applying the Design Thinking process. The research began with understanding user needs through online questionnaires and in-depth interviews. The data collected was analyzed and transformed into Customer Journey Maps and Empathy Maps to identify genuine problems and requirements. Through brainstorming sessions, solutions were generated and developed into an application prototype featuring key functionalities including 3D/AR tourist attraction recommendations, accommodation search and booking systems, restaurant recommendations, and navigation features. The satisfaction evaluation revealed high to very high levels of satisfaction across all aspects, particularly in user interface design and ease of use, with over 40% of users giving the highest ratings. This research not only demonstrates the effectiveness of the Design Thinking process in developing tourism applications but also presents a development approach that can be applied to future applications in the tourism industry.

articleTitle: Soil pH Measurement System Using Internet of Things (IoT) Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: The rapid advancement of Internet of Things (IoT) technology presents significant opportunities for improving agricultural practices, particularly in soil management. This research focuses on the development and evaluation of a soil pH measurement system integrated with IoT technology to aid farmers in monitoring and managing soil conditions. The system provides real-time, accurate soil pH data, which is essential for optimizing crop growth and productivity by ensuring optimal soil health. The prototype of the soil pH measurement system was developed and tested with a group of 30 farmers, who were asked to use the application and provide feedback on various aspects such as system design, ease of use, material quality, and data clarity. The results of the testing phase showed that the system was well-received by the users. The majority of respondents (85%) expressed satisfaction with the design and usability of the application. Furthermore, the system's real-time pH data, as well as the ability to generate clear and actionable reports, received high ratings from the users. The research also identified areas for further improvement, including the need to enhance the ease of use and optimize the user interface to accommodate a broader range of users. Overall, the findings demonstrate that IoT-based technology can significantly improve soil pH monitoring, providing farmers with the tools needed to make data-driven decisions. This, in turn, leads to better soil management practices, increased agricultural productivity, and more sustainable farming. This research underscores the potential of IoT technology in addressing critical agricultural challenges and offers a foundation for future developments of similar systems designed to enhance farm management practices globally. The insights gained from this study contribute to the growing body of knowledge in precision agriculture and can serve as a guide for the development of other IoT-based agricultural solutions.

articleTitle: Applying Machine Learning Techniques and Feature Selection Methods for Lung Cancer Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This research aims to apply several machine learning techniques, including Neural Networks, Random Forests, Naive Bayes, K-nearest Neighbors, and Decision Trees, to predict lung cancer. A dataset from the Kaggle database, consisting of 309 records and 16 features, was used to evaluate the performance of these ML algorithms. The models were compared based on their effectiveness with different feature selection methods. The results of the research showed that the Random Forest model was the most effective for predicting lung cancer. The Information Gain approach identified the 14 most suitable features and achieved the highest accuracy of 96.77%, precision of 96.80%, recall of 96.80%, f-measure of 96.80%, and RMSE of 0.2113. These results demonstrate how the proposed approach can improve prognostic and diagnostic systems for lung cancer treatment planning and decision-making. Early diagnosis and treatment of lung cancer can significantly reduce mortality rates.

articleTitle: A Review on Internet of Things Technologies for People with Disabilities
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: The Internet of Things (IoT) presents transformative opportunities to enhance accessibility and foster independence for individuals with disabilities. This paper provides a comprehensive review of IoT technologies designed for this purpose, exploring their applications in healthcare, education, and smart environments. It highlights the benefits of these technologies in promoting independence and social inclusion while addressing key challenges such as affordability, accessibility, and privacy. Additionally, it examines future directions for IoT and the potential of emerging technologies, such as edge computing and artificial intelligence, to further enhance its applications. This review aims to support the development of inclusive, affordable, and effective IoT systems that improve quality of life and enable meaningful societal participation for people with disabilities.

articleTitle: Knowledge Distillation Using Entropy-Guided Dynamic Parameter Transfer for Wound Image Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This study proposes a novel model compression approach for wound image classification using Knowledge Distillation (KD) enhanced by Entropy-Guided Adaptive Scaling (EGAS). EGAS comprises Entropy-Guided Adaptive Temperature Scaling (EGATS) and Entropy-Guided Adaptive Alpha Scaling (EGAAS), which dynamically adjust temperature and loss balancing based on entropy. Unlike traditional KD with fixed parameters, EGAS ensures smoother knowledge transfer for uncertain cases while preserving sharp distinctions for confident predictions. From Table VIII experimental results show that EGAS significantly improves classification accuracy, enabling the deployment of lightweight, high-performance models in resource-constrained environments for real-time medical applications.

articleTitle: Development of a PM2.5 Measurement Device Using Dust Sensors for Air Quality Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This research focuses on the development of an advanced air purifier system integrated with PM2.5 detection, UV-C light sterilization, and real-time monitoring through an IoT-based interface. The system utilizes a PM2.5 sensor to detect airborne particulate matter and activates the air purifier and UV-C light when the air quality exceeds predefined thresholds. Additionally, the system is designed to display PM2.5 values on an LCD screen and send notifications to a mobile application (LINE) to inform users about air quality conditions. Prototype testing was conducted in a 6 × 12-meter room using hairspray to simulate PM2.5 particles. The results showed that the air purifier activated successfully in response to elevated PM2.5 levels, displaying real-time data and sending alerts with messages such as “Danger” when air quality worsened. This study demonstrates the feasibility of combining IoT technology and real-time air quality monitoring to enhance environmental health management in indoor spaces. The proposed system provides a user-centric solution that not only improves air quality but also ensures immediate user awareness and intervention.

articleTitle: Automated Bounding Dimension Retrieval: A Machine Learning-Driven Framework for Engineering Drawing Interpretation
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: Accurately retrieving bounding dimensions from engineering drawings is critical for manufacturing processes, influencing machining feasibility, material selection, and cost estimation. This paper presents an innovative Automated Bounding Dimension Retrieval (ABDR) framework, integrating state-of-the-art object detection and Optical Character Recognition (OCR) technologies with a novel ratio-based analysis methodology. The proposed multi-stage pipeline systematically identifies primary, secondary, and tertiary dimensions across multiple views, addressing challenges such as view separation, bounding box detection, and text classification. The ABDR framework was evaluated on a dataset of engineering drawings adhering to ISO standards. The view detection module, implemented using YOLOv10n, achieved 98% mAP50, while the bounding box detection module using YOLOv11n reached 98.7% mAP50 and 97.5% mAP75. The text extraction module, employing EasyOCR, attained 83.55% accuracy and 95.87% normalized edit distance. The overall pipeline achieved 81% accuracy in dimension retrieval. By automating this traditionally manual and error-prone process, the ABDR framework provides a robust and scalable solution, offering significant advancements for technical drawing interpretation and manufacturing workflow automation.

articleTitle: A Semantic Approach to Clinical Risk Detection: Early Warning Systems with Knowledge Graphs
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: Detecting early signs of clinical deterioration is vital for ensuring patient safety and enabling timely intervention. This paper introduces a hybrid Early Warning System (EWS) that integrates physiological monitoring with semantic symp-tom reasoning to support clinical decision-making. The system leverages automated machine learning to identify nonlinear patterns in historical vital sign data, while a curated knowledge base links patient-reported symptoms to standardized clinical concepts. A conversational large language model guides user interaction, asking context-aware questions to clarify ambiguous input and improve data completeness. Once both physiological and symptom-based inputs are harmonized, the system generates an interpretable EWS score and suggests potential diagnoses or symptom clusters. This approach enhances predictive accuracy while maintaining transparency and promoting trust among clin-icians. By combining data-driven modeling with semantic reasoning and interactive AI, the proposed framework demonstrates a promising direction for human-centered, next-generation clinical decision support systems.

articleTitle: Road Incident Detection and Alert System for Immediate Assistance
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: In this paper, we have developed a road accident detection system using Image Processing techniques. The performance of three different models-CNN, Yolov8, and Dino DETR-was tested to determine which model provides the highest accuracy in detecting road accidents. The results of the experiments showed that the Dino DETR model outperformed both CNN and Yolov8, achieving an accuracy rate of 96%. This accuracy is approximately 7% higher than that of the CNN model and Yolov8, making it the most effective approach for detecting road accidents in this study. The findings of this study highlight the potential of using the Dino DETR model in road accident detection systems. With a detection accuracy of 96%, this model demonstrates significant promise for real-world applications, where quick and accurate accident detection is crucial for timely assistance and response. The successful implementation of such systems could significantly improve road safety, reduce accident-related fatalities and injuries, and enhance the efficiency of emergency response services. This research lays the groundwork for future developments in automated traffic monitoring systems that can assist in preventing road accidents and minimizing their impact.

articleTitle: An Integration of User-Centered Design and Design Thinking Principles for Developing a Mobile Application for Nutritional Tracking for Thai Elderly: A Mixed-Method Study
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: The growing elderly population presents significant challenges for health and nutrition management, particularly in maintaining dietary balance and nutrient intake. This study aims to develop a mobile nutrition calculator application tailored to elderly users by integrating User-Centered Design (UCD) and Design Thinking methodologies. The research employs a mixed-method approach comprising five phases: context analysis, requirement specification, user modeling, interface design, and usability testing. A total of 30 elderly participants were engaged through interviews, prototyping, and usability testing. Findings highlight critical usability issues specific to the elderly, including visual, cognitive, and interactional limitations. The application was developed using Kotlin and Firebase, with interface elements designed via Figma to ensure clarity and accessibility. Usability results showed high satisfaction (Mean=4.42, SD=0.51) and effective user engagement, with the integrated design approach outperforming conventional development strategies. This study contributes a practical framework for age-friendly digital health design, emphasizing the synergistic strengths of UCD and Design Thinking in addressing elderly-specific usability needs. The findings offer insights for developers, researchers, and health practitioners seeking to improve digital health tools for aging populations.

articleTitle: Leveraging Knowledge Graphs for Personalized Internship Recommendations: A Case Study on Software Engineering Courses
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: Internships play a vital role in bridging academic learning with industry requirements. This paper presents a knowledge graph-based framework for generating personalized internship recommendations by integrating course syllabi, student competencies, and job descriptions. The approach leverages structured knowledge representation and graph traversal to dynamically match students' academic progress with relevant opportunities. Additionally, Large Language Models (LLMs) are employed for entity extraction to enhance recommendation accuracy. A case study involving Software Engineering subjects within a Programme of Innovative Engineering demonstrates the framework's ability to provide tailored internship suggestions and identify skill gaps. The results indicate that knowledge graphs offer a scalable and adaptable solution for aligning academic curricula with evolving industry needs.

articleTitle: Object Detection for Assistive Technology: A Comprehensive Real-World Performance Evaluation using a Dedicated Framework
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This study explores the feasibility of using object detection technology to aid visually impaired individuals by providing real-time information about the surrounding environment. Recognizing the challenges faced by millions worldwide with visual impairments, this research investigates the potential of object detection systems to provide crucial, real-time environmental awareness. A custom framework was developed to facilitate data collection and analysis, using data from both real-time device operation and diverse image datasets. This approach allowed for a comprehensive evaluation of performance accuracy and reliability in realistic, real-world settings. The research assesses the capabilities and limitations of object detection for assistive technology, focusing on its potential to accurately identify and locate objects critical for navigation and interaction. Two representative models were evaluated: YOLOv11, chosen for compute-intensive tasks, and KidBright μAI, a representative platform for edge AI deployment. YOLOv11, running on Raspberry Pi 5, demonstrated strong performance with an average F1-score of 0.7762, precision of 0.9380, and recall of 0.8100, but required 3.40 J per inference. KidBright μAI, designed for edge computing, achieved an F1-score of 0.5992, precision of 0.5621, and recall of 0.6383, with a significantly lower energy consumption of 0.21 J per cycle. In user trials, the assistive device, utilizing YOLOv11 due to its higher precision and lower false positives, improved object localization success rates from 50% to 85.7<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">%</sup> for visually impaired participants. The findings highlight the potential of object detection for assistive technology, with YOLOv11 offering higher accuracy and KidBright μAI providing a more energy-efficient solution.

articleTitle: Integration of Problem Solution Design Framework and Design Thinking
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This research presents the Problem Solution Design Framework as a tool developed to enhance the effectiveness of the design thinking process in innovative business solution development by adding systematic analysis and business feasibility assessment dimensions. The research employed a controlled experimental design with pre-test and post-test, involving 60 students divided into control and experimental groups of 30 students each, conducted over a 7-day period. Data was collected across four dimensions: process efficiency, solution quality, development time, and user satisfaction. Results showed that the experimental group achieved significantly higher post-test scores of 80.27 compared to 78.17 in the control group. Expert evaluation revealed that the experimental group achieved a higher overall mean score of 4.21 compared to 3.95, particularly in problem understanding and time management. Students in the experimental group also reported higher satisfaction scores of 4.19 compared to 3.87. These findings demonstrate that the proposed framework can significantly enhance business solution development efficiency. This research contributes significantly to developing entrepreneurship teaching methods and provides guidelines for organizations in business innovation development.

articleTitle: Modeling Urban Transformation and Predicting Respiratory Disease Trends in Thailand with Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This study investigates how urban environmental, social, and economic factors influence the prevalence of respiratory diseases across nine provinces in Thailand. Utilizing data from 2017 to 2021, various regression models were tested to forecast respiratory disease cases in 2023. The optimized Random Forest Regression model was identified as the most accurate, achieving an R2 Score of 0.82, MAE of 160.45, and RMSE of 185.32. These results highlight the role of urbanization in respiratory health trends and provide insights for policymakers to mitigate health risks. The findings emphasize the necessity for improved urban planning and environmental management to minimize adverse health impacts and highlight the potential of machine learning techniques for time-series health forecasting.

articleTitle: Abortion Follow-Up Framework for Healthcare Management
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: Post-abortion care is the medical treatment process for ensuring the well-being and recovery of patients after abortion. Nevertheless, gathering information from the discharged patients to assess and monitor potential complications can be challenging. In this paper, we propose designing and implementing healthcare management tool to enable the self-assessment of discharged patient to identify her post-abortion condition and provide an opportunity for healthcare officers to surveillance the potential complications of patients after abortion. The objective is to establish a methodology for actively interacting between discharged patients and the healthcare officer. The abortion follow-up framework facilitates the healthcare officers to collect the discharged patient conditions and automatically assess potential complications and diseases associated with post-abortion recovery. The discharged patients will receive a post-abortion guideline along with an individualized quick response code to access the self-assessment feature. The participants are ninetytwo abortion patients who have approved consent for sensitive data collection as volunteers for preliminary use. The self-assessment result demonstrates that twenty-two abnormal cases required the healthcare officer to observe the early warning sign of potential complications during post-abortion surveillance. The abnormal cases are 14.23 percent of the first follow-up time and 9.78 percent of the second follow-up time. The positive feedback and high average Likert scale ratings received from respondents illustrate a very satisfactory level after using the framework.

articleTitle: A Comparative Study for Effectiveness of Different Artificial Intelligence Models for Thai Lettuce Price Prediction
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: Agriculture is one of the most important sectors in Thailand. Many farmers face challenges in crop pricing due to the fluctuation of the agricultural product market. Research on how to create an optimal crop portfolio suggests that accurate price predictions can help farmers choose the most profitable crops, thus solving this problem. In this research, we test different machine learning models, including Random Forest, XGBoost, and LSTM, to predict agricultural product, in this case Thai Lettuce prices. We use past price and meteorological data to train the models. The results show that LSTM performs better than the other models, achieving the lowest MSE (44.45), RMSE (6.67), and MAE (5.33). Additionally, LSTM provides a better fit to the data compared to Random Forest and XGBoost, which show lower predictive capabilities. These findings highlight LSTM's potential as a reliable model for agricultural price prediction, offering valuable insights to help farmers make better-informed decisions.

articleTitle: Altitude Hold Controls on Multi-Rotor sUAV with Barometer Effects
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This paper presents an accurate altitude estimation on a small multirotor UAV. That is crucial for the stability and performance of UAV, particularly in altitude hold control. Barometric pressure sensors are widely used to estimate altitude based on atmospheric pressure, but their readings are highly susceptible to environmental fluctuations, temperature variations, and dynamic airflow effects. To mitigate these altitude errors, this study focuses on enhanced flight control installation techniques, including the physical protection of barometric sensors inside enclosed, well-ventilated compartments to shield them from wind disturbances and rapid pressure changes. The proposed mitigation strategy is validated through ground testing and flight testing, where altitude hold performance is assessed under various environmental conditions. The results confirm that enclosing the barometric sensor within a protective, ventilated chamber significantly reduces altitude estimation errors, leading to more stable altitude hold control with reduced vertical oscillations. These findings highlight the importance of integrated sensor protection in UAV flight control system design and provide a practical framework for improving altitude estimation reliability in both consumer and industrial UAV applications.

articleTitle: Innovative Solutions in Breath Alcohol Measurement for Improving Road Safety
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This research presents the development and evaluation of a breath alcohol measurement device utilizing the MQ-3 alcohol sensor and an Arduino Nano-based control system. The primary objective was to design an accurate and reliable system for detecting breath alcohol concentration, with real-time feedback provided through an OLED display and an active buzzer for alerts. The device operates by measuring the alcohol concentration in the breath and converting the sensor data into parts per million (ppm). When the alcohol concentration exceeds the predefined threshold of 5% ABV, the system activates an audible alarm via the buzzer and displays the corresponding ppm value on the OLED screen. A series of tests were conducted with eight volunteers who consumed varying amounts of alcohol. The results demonstrated the system's high accuracy and responsiveness, with the ability to detect alcohol concentrations ranging from safe levels to dangerous thresholds. The device was tested multiple times to ensure consistency and minimize errors, with the final results confirming its effectiveness in providing reliable alcohol measurements. This system holds significant potential for applications in monitoring alcohol levels in drivers and individuals involved in safety-critical activities. The research underscores the importance of real-time alcohol detection systems in enhancing public safety and ensuring compliance with safety regulations.

articleTitle: Vertical Farming with Smart Technology to Increase Agricultural Productivity
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This research presents the design and development of an innovative prototype for vertical farming that can be controlled through smart technology to increase the amount of agricultural products to achieve food security. By designing and developing innovative prototypes for growing vertical agricultural crops that are controlled through an internet-based application. To control the environment anytime, anywhere as desired. Using temperature and humidity control with a microcontroller and develop applications that can be controlled via Android smartphones. Let's increase the efficiency of growing hydroponic salad vegetables. To increase the quality and weight of the salad vegetables. As a result, the farmers earn more income per month, which is a career that is suitable for conditions and areas with limited water sources and resources. We chose the green oak vegetables to make and experiment because green oak vegetables are popular for consumption and can be grown and harvested all year round. In addition, it is a salad vegetable with a relatively high price per kilogram. In addition, the recorded parameters that are important to plant growth for a period of 9 months, starting from June 2023 to February 2024, by specifying important parameters for recording data such as air temperature, humidity, water temperature, amount of light, control value, electrical conductivity of plant nutrient solution, pH value of water and the concentration of the solution in the water. The results of found that growing in the same area between hydroponic growing with general horizontal rails and growing with a vertical farming prototype at a size of 1.00 x 1.50 meters, it was found that growing with the vertical farming prototype could grow 40 plants, but growing with general horizontal rails could grow 32–35 plants. The weight of vegetables grown with the vertical farming prototype and controlled environment gave higher yield than the hydroponic growing method with general horizontal rails by 29.1%, which led to income and profits that farmers would receive.

articleTitle: EEG2Face Query: Retrieving Facial Imagery from EEG Signals with Latent Embeddings
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: Electroencephalography (EEG) has been widely applied in various fields, such as controlling robotic arms for individuals with disabilities and analyzing patients' emotions and mental states. One interesting application is using EEG signals for image retrieval in databases based on human thoughts. This project focuses on enhancing the efficiency of facial image retrieval based on users' mental imagery by utilizing EEG signals. It utilizes the Ultracortex Mark IV headset equipped with 16 sensor points, combined with machine learning techniques, to retrieve facial images that match the user's thoughts. This approach demonstrates the potential of EEG signals in bridging the gap between thought processes and image retrieval, offering new advancements in neuroscience and technology.

articleTitle: Application “Here We Go”: An Innovative App for Enhancing Social Interaction in the Digital Age
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This research presents the development of the Here We Go application, designed to address social interaction challenges and facilitate activity-based friendships through the Design Thinking process. The research methodology involved comprehensive user needs analysis through an online survey with 100 participants and in-depth interviews with 10 participants, leading to the development of key features including a secure identity verification system, activity creation and participation modules, an integrated chat system, partner store recommendations, and an innovative Chatbot for stress counseling. The application underwent rigorous testing with a sample group, demonstrating high user satisfaction particularly in terms of security and usability, with subsequent improvements implemented based on user feedback. The research findings conclusively show that the Here We Go application effectively addresses social interaction challenges and facilitates relationship building through various activities, while maintaining a strong focus on user security and experience. This successful integration of social connectivity features with robust security measures represents a significant contribution to solving modern social interaction challenges in the digital age, making it a valuable tool for individuals seeking meaningful social connections through shared activities.

articleTitle: Multi-Factor Authentication for Web Applications Using JWT and Face Embedding-Based Recognition
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: Stateless authentication using JSON Web Tokens (JWT) has become widely adopted in web applications over the past decade. Typically, this method relies on a single authentication factor, namely a username and password, which makes it vulnerable to password theft. This paper proposes a multi-factor authentication system that integrates JWT with face recognition for enhanced security. The first step involves user authentication via username and password using JWT. Next, face identification is performed using a face embedding approach on the web page. If both authentication factors are validated successfully, the user is granted access to protected resources. The system is implemented as a web authentication prototype for experimental validation. The dataset includes 30 individuals, each with 15 facial images, resulting in a total of 450 facial images. Additionally, 100 unknown faces are used for evaluating the system's performance on an unknown class. The results show high accuracy in face identification, with an overall performance metric of 0.95.

articleTitle: Senior-Safety-Strider: AI-Powered Walking Aid with Fall Detection for Seniors
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This research presents the analysis and evaluation of an AI-powered walking aid system, which utilizes pitch and roll angle data from a cane to monitor and assess user walking behavior. The system is designed to distinguish between correct and incorrect walking behaviors by analyzing changes in these angles during user movement. The experimental results indicate that when the roll angle of the cane increases beyond 8 degrees while the pitch angle remains within the range of −20 to 20 degrees, the movement is identified as correct walking behavior, allowing the system to accurately count steps. However, if the pitch angle deviates beyond the specified range and the roll angle shows significant changes, the system identifies the walking behavior as incorrect and halts analysis to prevent inaccurate step counting. The findings of this study demonstrate that the AI-powered walking aid system effectively detects and analyzes walking behavior, thereby enhancing walking safety and preventing falls for users, particularly among the elderly who require appropriate and continuous care and support.

articleTitle: Needs Analysis for Developing Intelligent Digital Platform for Course Learning Outcome Assessment of Information Technology Program in Higher Education
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This study aims to analyze the requirements for developing an intelligent digital platform for assessing Course Learning Outcomes (CLO) in undergraduate Information Technology programs within the framework of Outcome-Based Education (OBE). Traditional CLO assessment methods face several limitations, such as time-consuming manual evaluation and a lack of in-depth analysis for timely instructional improvement. This study explores expectations and key functions of the digital platform through surveys conducted among faculty members, students, and administrators. The findings indicate that students and faculty prioritize the need for an Artificial Intelligence Assessment System (AAS), while administrators emphasize the importance of a Reporting and Visualization System (RVS). These preferences align with expert evaluations, which identified the AAS as having the highest mean score (4.73), followed closely by the RVS (4.72). The overall mean score across all six components of the platform was 4.58, indicating a high level of importance. This research provides a foundational framework for developing an intelligent digital platform for CLO assessment in undergraduate Information Technology programs. Beyond facilitating learning outcome assessments, the platform has the potential to enhance the quality and efficiency of higher education teaching and learning in the future.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning Framework for Diabetes Detection Using Hoeffding Tree
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This research aims to classify diabetes patients using machine learning algorithms, with a particular focus on the Hoeffding Tree model. The study utilizes a dataset comprising 256,380 samples, categorized based on ten key health and demographic attributes: (1) history of stroke, (2) daily vegetable consumption, (3) heavy alcohol consumption, (4) health insurance coverage, (5) inability to afford medical consultation in the past 12 months, (6) self-rated general health status (ranging from excellent to poor), (7) difficulty in walking or climbing stairs, (8) gender (male, female), (9) educational attainment (from never attended school to college graduate), and (10) classification type. The objective is to develop a standardized and efficient diabetes classification model that reduces diagnostic time and optimizes resource allocation. Before selecting the Hoeffding Tree as the primary model, the research team conducted a comprehensive evaluation of 27 machine learning algorithms. The Hoeffding Tree demonstrated the highest classification performance, achieving an accuracy of 85.9528%. The findings highlight the model's effectiveness in diabetes classification and its potential for practical implementation in healthcare decision-making.

articleTitle: Phishing URL Detection Using Machine Learning and Deep Learning in NLP
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: Phishing attacks are an emerging cyber threat that makes use of fake URLs to pilfer sensitive information of users, such as their login credentials and other financial details. In line with this, the present study involves the adoption of NLP methods with machine-learning algorithms in effectively detecting phishing URLs. To this end, five different algorithms are considered for effectiveness in the study: LSTM, GRU, Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, and Logistic Regression. Each of them was trained and then tested with a complete dataset, containing phishing and legitimate URLs for correctness in distinguishing malicious URLs from the benign ones.
