Amongst them, the LSTM model recorded an accuracy as high as 98% due to its capability for handling sequential dependencies in addition to contextual patterns within the URLs. This research underlines the promise of LSTM-based models in fighting phishing threats and further proposes a scalable solution to enable real-time phishing URL detection and enhance cybersecurity defense.

articleTitle: Comparison of Milk Quality Grades Using the Logistic Model Tree Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This study aims to track and categorize milk quality grades using the Logistic Model Tree (LMT) algorithm, based on the analysis of 1,059 milk samples. The focus of the research is to evaluate key factors such as pH value, taste, smell, fat content, concentration, and color, which play a crucial role in determining the overall quality of milk. The goal is to create an efficient and standardized process for sorting cow's milk, which can save significant time and resources in the dairy industry. To identify the most suitable algorithm for this task, the research team initially tested 12 different algorithms, assessing their performance in predicting milk quality. Among these, the Logistic Model Tree (LMT) emerged as the most effective model, achieving an impressive accuracy rate of 99.76%. The LMT algorithm, known for combining the advantages of decision trees and logistic regression, demonstrated its ability to classify milk quality grades with high precision. The results of this study indicate that the LMT algorithm can be a valuable tool for automating the milk quality grading process. By leveraging key attributes such as pH, fat content, and color, it is possible to efficiently sort and grade milk, reducing the need for manual inspection and improving overall productivity in the dairy industry. This method offers a significant improvement over traditional quality assessment techniques and has the potential to be widely adopted for milk sorting and quality control applications.

articleTitle: Development of a System for Measuring pH and Oxygen Levels in Water Using Internet of Things (IoT) Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This paper presents the development of an automated water quality control system aimed at optimizing conditions for fish farming. The system is designed to measure and adjust key water parameters, including pH, oxygen levels, and temperature, to ensure an ideal environment for fish. The main objectives include measuring the water pH before chemical adjustment, regulating pH to suitable levels for aquaculture, monitoring oxygen levels to maintain an adequate supply, and controlling water temperature to ensure stable conditions. The system employs sensors to monitor pH and temperature, with the ability to trigger specific actions based on predefined conditions. For example, if the pH exceeds 5.0 and the temperature exceeds the threshold, both the LED light and DC motor operate to improve water quality. Conversely, if the pH drops below 5.0 or the temperature is below the desired range, the system adjusts accordingly. The integration of these functions into a unified system provides real-time water quality management, enhancing the sustainability and efficiency of aquaculture operations. The proposed system demonstrates a practical solution for improving water quality control in fish farming, ensuring the health of aquatic life while optimizing resource use.

articleTitle: myNER: Contextualized Burmese Named Entity Recognition with Bidirectional LSTM and fastText Embeddings via Joint Training with POS Tagging
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: Named Entity Recognition (NER) involves identifying and categorizing named entities within textual data. Despite its significance, NER research has often overlooked low-resource languages like Myanmar (Burmese), primarily due to the lack of publicly available annotated datasets. To address this, we introduce <tex xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">$\boldsymbol{m}\boldsymbol{y}\boldsymbol{N}\boldsymbol{E}\boldsymbol{R}$</tex>, a novel word-level NER corpus featuring a 7-tag annotation scheme, enriched with Part-of-Speech (POS) tagging to provide additional syntactic information. Alongside the corpus, we conduct a comprehensive evaluation of NER models, including Conditional Random Fields (CRF), Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM)-CRF, and their combinations with fastText embeddings in different settings. Our experiments reveal the effectiveness of contextualized word embeddings and the impact of joint training with POS tagging, demonstrating significant performance improvements across models. The traditional CRF joint-task model with fastText embeddings as a feature achieved the best result, with a 0.9818 accuracy and 0.9811 weighted F1 score with 0.7429 macro F1 score. BiLSTM-CRF with fine-tuned fastText embeddings gets the best result of 0.9791 accuracy and 0.9776 weighted F1 score with 0.7395 macro F1 score.

articleTitle: Analysis on Business Model Innovation for Industrial Business Integrated Future Research
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: Business Model Innovation (BMI) extensively is developing of business model on attention academic and practitioners. The gap of BMI research is fragmented and inconsistent, lacking a comprehensive and systematic framework. This study purposes to conduct literature reviews from published between 2010 and 2024. The methodology uses analysis on five dimensions: antecedents, processes, barriers, outcomes, and moderators/mediators of BMI. That synthesizes the findings and proposes integrated theories the captures the complex relationship on these dimensions for future studies advantages. This study contributes to rapid change in research by providing clear guidance as a generality model in the future.

articleTitle: Tourism Chatbot Framework: Enhancing Visitor Experience Through GraphRAG and AI Chatbot
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This study introduces a tourism chatbot frame-work based on the GraphRAG approach, designed to enhance visitor engagement through personalized recommendations for attractions, local products, and travel routes in Rayong, Thailand. By integrating Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) with a tourism knowledge graph, the chatbot leverages both LLMs and structured data to deliver accurate, context-aware responses. The knowledge graph, built using Navanurak platform data, preserves Thailand's cultural heritage and biodiversity information, enriching the chatbots insights. The framework employs a hybrid search strategy, combining structured data retrieval and vector similarity search, enabling real-time, human-like interactions. Evaluation results show high precision, recall, and F1 scores for both location-based and general queries, demonstrating the chatbot's potential to promote lesser-known destinations and support local economies. This study highlights the effectiveness of integrating knowledge graphs with RAG to improve tourism experiences through enhanced information accessibility and personalization.

articleTitle: BERT-Based Semantic Retrieval for Academic Abstracts
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This research focuses on improving the academic abstract search system to help reduce search time and facilitate users in searching with general terms, without the need for specific terminology, and using synonyms in the search. We evaluated the performance of four techniques: TF-IDF, Doc2Vec, Word2Vec, and BERT, through experiments using a dataset of 10,000 abstracts in the field of science and technology, which were embedded using the four techniques. The main objective is the accuracy of using keywords to search for the four techniques, which then yield abstracts that correctly match the 100 prepared abstracts before the search. This serves as a basis for developing an efficient techniques for future academic abstract search systems.

articleTitle: An Enhanced Chatbot for University Admission and Educational Guidance
publicationTitle: 2025 IEEE International Conference on Cybernetics and Innovations (ICCI)
abstract: This study presents evidence to support students to university admission services due to a shortage of staff. The chatbot was developed using machine learning and natural language processing and was tested on the LINE application. The developed chatbot can provide low-cost support for admission, tuition fees, and contextual questions in a personalized and speedy manner. A mixed-method approach was applied, merging qualitative and quantitative data to optimize performance. Further, a usability test of 100 students yielded results of a 92% satisfaction rate. The accuracy assessment results provide 97% accuracy, with an F1 score of 82%. These reflect how effective chatbots are in enhancing user experience while lessening dependence on human advisors, hence smoothing workflow processes when providing educational support. Results show how AI has transformed education through efficiency, integration, and access. This study found a basis for scaling AI applications in higher education and other services focusing on students.
